title: Comparison of global cohomology
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a finite discrete ring, with left $\Lambda$-module sheaves. For $K\in\Dplus(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the unit $\eta_K:K	o R
u_{T,*}
u_T^*K$ of the bounded-below derived comparison adjunction [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] induces a natural isomorphism
$$
 R\Gamma(T_{\Et},K)\xrightarrow{\sim}
 R\Gamma(T_{\Proet},
u_T^*K).
$$
This is the composite of $R\Gamma(T_{\Et},\eta_K)$ with the canonical final-object comparison $R\Gamma(T_{\Et},R
u_{T,*}
u_T^*K)\cong R\Gamma(T_{\Proet},
u_T^*K)$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-sections-pushforward]. Both section functors are ordinary right-derived sections at the terminal objects, with the etale construction of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

proof.text: For a bounded-below complex J of pro-etale Λ-module sheaves, exactness of ν_T^* from [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] implies that its right adjoint ν_{T,*} preserves injectives. Resolving J by injectives, ν_{T,*} computes the derived direct image, and evaluation on the final object identifies Γ(T_Et,ν_{T,*}J^r) with Γ(T_Proet,J^r) termwise. Therefore the derived-sections identity RΓ(T_Et,Rν_{T,*}J) ≅ RΓ(T_Proet,J) is the preceding node.

proof.text: Apply that identity to J=ν_T^*K. The derived unit K→Rν_{T,*}ν_T^*K is an isomorphism by [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], so applying RΓ(T_Et,−) gives the claimed natural isomorphism RΓ(T_Et,K) ≅ RΓ(T_Proet,ν_T^*K).

The recorded etale coefficient definition is commutative-ring-valued, while the finite-level comparison and its source context allow arbitrary finite rings and left modules. The corrected text explicitly fixes that coefficient convention and specifies the previously unnamed canonical final-object comparison used after the derived unit, adding its existing DAG node to statement dependencies. This changes no mathematical hypothesis relative to the source context and imposes no commutativity assumption.
